q: 1. A plain scale is used to read
explain: A plain scale has graduations in only one direction, so it can represent lengths in one unit and its sub-division (i.e., two dimensions like metres and decimetres), not areas or volumes.

q: 2. A diagonal scale is used to read ... dimensions
explain: A diagonal scale uses diagonal lines to subdivide the smallest division further, allowing three successive dimensions (units, tenths, hundredths) to be read directly.

q: 3. A scale which has a common representative fraction, but read in different measures, is called a
explain: A comparative scale shares the same representative fraction as another scale but is graduated in a different unit of measurement (e.g., miles and kilometres), enabling direct comparison.

q: 4. In a direct vernier, the smallest division of a vernier is ... the smallest division of its primary scale
explain: In a direct vernier, the vernier scale graduations are slightly shorter than the main scale graduations, and they increase in the same direction, allowing finer readings.

q: 5. Measurements taken with a wrong scale can be corrected by using the relation
options: true length = (correct scale/wrong scale) x measured length
true length = (correct scale/wrong scale)^2 x measured length
true length = (correct scale/wrong scale)^3 x measured length
explain: For linear measurements taken with a wrong scale, the correct relation is true length = (wrong scale/correct scale) x measured length; the given options invert this ratio, so none of these matches the correct formula.

q: 6. If x is the smallest division on the main scale and n are the number of divisions on the vernier, then the least count of the vernier is
explain: The least count of a vernier equals the smallest main scale division divided by the total number of divisions on the vernier scale, i.e., x/n.

q: 7. An average length of a pace is
explain: An average human pace (step length) while walking normally is taken as approximately 0.8 m (80 cm) for rough distance estimation in surveying.

q: 8. The method of measuring distance by pacing is chiefly used in
explain: Pacing gives only approximate distances and is used mainly during reconnaissance surveys, where a quick rough idea of the terrain and distances is needed before detailed survey work.

q: 9. Deviation of the actual road gradient from the proposed contour gradient uphill side, involves
options: earth work on the centre line
explain: When the actual ground rises above (uphill of) the proposed contour gradient line, material must be excavated from the centre line to bring the road to the designed level.

q: 10. Two hill tops A and B 20 km apart are intervened by a third top C. If the top most contour of the three hill tops are of the same value, state whether the line of sight AB
options: passes below the hill top C
passes below the hill top C
explain: If all three hill tops have the same elevation, and C lies between A and B, the line of sight AB just touches (grazes) hill top C due to the curvature of the earth affecting the intermediate point differently.

q: 11. The best method of interpolation of contours, is by
explain: Graphical interpolation (using a series of parallel equally-spaced lines or a tracing paper method) is the most accurate and commonly preferred method of interpolating contour points.

q: 12. For preparation of contour plan for a route survey
options: method of trace contour is used
method of cross profile is used
indirect method of contouring is used
explain: For route surveys (roads, railways), contour plans are prepared using cross-sections taken perpendicular to the centre line, i.e., the method of cross profile.

q: 13. Accuracy of elevation of various points obtained from contour map is limited to
explain: The accuracy of elevations read from a contour map is generally limited to about half (1/2) of the contour interval, since contours are drawn at discrete intervals.

q: 14. While surveying a plot of land by plane tabling, the field observations
options: and plotting do not proceed simultaneously
and recorded in field books to be plotted later
explain: Plane tabling is unique among surveying methods in that field observation and plotting happen simultaneously on the table sheet in the field itself, eliminating the need for a separate field book.

q: 15. The distance between steps for measuring downhill to obtain better accuracy
options: decreases with decrease of weight of the chain
explain: On steeper downhill slopes, shorter measuring steps must be taken to maintain accuracy in stepping/chaining, so the step distance decreases as slope increases.

q: 16. If a tacheometer is fitted with an anallatic lens
options: additive constant is 100, multiplying constant is zero
multiplying constant is 100, additive constant is zero
both multiplying and additive constants are 100
both multiplying and additive constants are 50
explain: An anallatic lens is specifically introduced in the telescope to make the additive constant of the tacheometer zero, while the multiplying constant is kept at the standard value of 100.

q: 17. In an adjusted level, when the bubble is central, the axis of the bubble tube becomes parallel to
explain: In a properly adjusted level, when the bubble is centred, the bubble tube axis is parallel to the line of sight, ensuring horizontal sighting.

q: 18. Height of instrument method of leveling is
options: more accurate than rise and fall method
less accurate than rise and fall method
quicker and less tedious for large number of intermediate sights
explain: The height of instrument (HI) method requires fewer calculations per intermediate sight compared to the rise and fall method, making it quicker and less tedious when many intermediate sights are involved.

q: 19. The shape of vertical curve generally provided is
explain: Vertical curves connecting two gradients are generally designed as parabolic curves because they provide a constant rate of change of grade and are easy to compute and set out.

q: 20. An instrument used for ranging is
explain: A line ranger is an instrument specifically designed to establish intermediate points in line between two stations that may not be intervisible, i.e., for ranging.

q: 21. Survey plotting can be done with an accuracy of
explain: With good drafting instruments and practice, survey plotting can typically achieve an accuracy of about 0.25 mm on the plotted sheet.

q: 22. In a quadrantal system, the bearing of a line is measured
options: always clockwise from the south point of the reference meridian towards the line round the circle
clockwise or anticlockwise from the east or west whichever is nearer the line towards north or south
clockwise or anticlockwise from the north or south whichever is nearer the line towards east or west
explain: In the quadrantal bearing system, bearings are measured from the north or south, whichever is nearer, either clockwise or anticlockwise towards the east or west, and expressed within 0-90 degrees.

q: 23. In a whole circle bearing system N25 15'W corresponds to
explain: N25 15'W in WCB is measured clockwise from north (0 degrees): 360 - 25 15' = 334 45'.

q: 24. If the fore bearing of a line is 36 15', its back bearing will be
explain: Back bearing = fore bearing + 180 degrees (since fore bearing is less than 180 degrees): 36 15' + 180 = 216 15'.

q: 25. If the fore bearing of a line is N26 35'W, its back bearing will be
explain: To reverse a quadrantal bearing, the N/S letter and E/W letter are both swapped while the angle stays the same: N26 35'W becomes S26 35'E.

q: 26. When the whole circle bearing of two lines AB and AC are 115 and 41 respectively then the included angle BAC will be
explain: The included angle BAC is the difference between the two bearings measured from the common station A: 115 - 41 = 74.

q: 27. The horizontal angle between the true meridian and a survey line is called
explain: Azimuth is defined as the horizontal angle measured from the true (geographic) meridian to a survey line, usually measured clockwise.

q: 28. The horizontal angle between the truth meridian and magnetic meridian is known as
explain: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between the true meridian and the magnetic meridian at a given place and time.

q: 29. At the equator, the amount of dip is
explain: Dip is the vertical angle the magnetic needle makes with the horizontal; at the magnetic equator, the needle stays horizontal, so dip is 0 degrees.

q: 30. Usefullness of plane table is enhanced by providing
explain: The Indian tangent clinometer, when fitted to the alidade, allows vertical angles and elevations to be measured directly during plane tabling, enhancing its usefulness.

q: 31. For the revision of an existing survey with the help of plane table we generally use
explain: Resection allows the plane table position to be located and oriented using already known points on an existing map, making it ideal for revising existing surveys.

q: 32. A point determined by resection on a plane table is called
explain: When the position of the plane table station is determined by resection from known points, the resulting located point is termed a 'plane table fix'.

q: 33. The instrument which is used in plane tabling for obtaining horizontal and vertical distance directly without resorting to chaining, is known as
explain: A telescope alidade, fitted with stadia hairs, allows both horizontal and vertical distances to be measured tacheometrically directly during plane tabling, without chaining.

q: 34. The operation of revolving a plane table about its vertical axis so that all lines on the sheet become parallel to corresponding lines on the ground, is known
explain: Orientation is the process of rotating the plane table so that all lines on the plotted sheet remain parallel to their corresponding lines on the ground.

q: 35. In setting up a plane table at any station
options: both leveling and centering are done simultaneously
explain: When setting up a plane table, leveling and centering are carried out together (simultaneously) as adjustments to one affect the other.

q: 36. In tacheometrical observations, vertical staff holding is generally preferred to normal staffing, due to
options: minimum effect of careless holding on the result
explain: Vertical staff holding is preferred because small errors in tilting a vertically-held staff have minimal effect on the tacheometric distance/elevation results, unlike a normal (staff-held perpendicular to line of sight) approach.

q: 37. In tangential tacheometry, an ordinary level staff is used
options: leaning towards the instrument for inclined sights upward
leaning away from the instrument for inclined sights downwards
explain: In tangential tacheometry, the ordinary level staff is held vertical in all cases, and two vertical angles are observed to the top and bottom targets to compute distance.

q: 38. Horizontal distances obtained tacheometerically are corrected for
explain: Tacheometrically obtained horizontal distances (for long sights) need correction for the combined effect of earth's curvature and atmospheric refraction.

q: 39. Tilt of the staff in stadia tacheometry increases the intercept if it is
options: away from the telescope pointing down hill
away from the telescope pointing up-hill
explain: When the staff, held for an upward inclined sight, tilts away from the telescope, the staff intercept as seen by the stadia hairs is effectively lengthened, increasing the intercept.

q: 40. The intercept of a staff
options: is maximum if the staff is held truly normal to the line of sight
is minimum if the staff is held truly normal to the line of sight
decreases if the staff is tilted away from normal
increases if the staff is tilted towards normal
explain: When the staff is held exactly normal (perpendicular) to the line of sight, the staff intercept recorded is at its minimum value for that sight; any tilt away from normal increases the apparent intercept.

q: 41. If vertical angles of inclined sights do not exceed 10 and non-verticality of the staff is within 1, stadia system of tacheometric observations are made on
options: staff normal as well as vertical
explain: For small vertical angles (under 10 degrees) with limited non-verticality (within 1 degree), the staff is generally held normal to the line of sight in stadia tacheometry for simpler direct distance computation.

q: 42. The vertical distance above or below the datum is called
explain: The vertical distance of a point above or below the chosen datum is termed either its reduced level (RL) or its elevation - both terms are used interchangeably in leveling.

q: 43. A back sight indicates the ... of the instrument
explain: A back sight (BS), taken on a point of known elevation, is used to determine the height of the instrument (HI) above the datum.

q: 44. Imaginary line passing through points having equal magnetic declination is termed as
explain: An isogonic line (isogon) is a line on a map joining places having the same value of magnetic declination at a given time.

q: 45. Magnetic declination at any place
explain: Magnetic declination at any place is not constant; it changes gradually over time due to secular variation, as well as smaller diurnal and irregular variations.

q: 46. Sensitiveness of a level tube is designated by
options: length of bubble of level tube
explain: The sensitivity of a bubble/level tube is directly related to the radius of curvature of its inner surface; a larger radius gives a more sensitive tube.

q: 47. Dumpy level is most suitable when
options: the instrument is to be shifted frequently
fly leveling is being done over long distance
many readings are to be taken from a single setting of instrument
explain: A dumpy level, being simple and quick to set up but requiring re-leveling if moved, is best suited where many readings can be taken from one setup rather than frequent shifting.

q: 48. The correction for sag is
explain: Sag in a tape suspended between supports always causes the measured length to be longer than the true straight-line distance, so the sag correction is always subtractive.

q: 49. Number of links per metre length of a chain are
explain: In a standard metric chain, there are 5 links per metre length, so a 20 m chain has 100 links and a 30 m chain has 150 links.

q: 50. Cross-staff is used for
explain: A cross-staff is a simple hand instrument used in chain surveying to set out right angles (perpendicular offsets) from the chain line.

q: 51. Pantagraph is used for
explain: A pantograph is a mechanical linkage instrument used to copy, enlarge, or reduce plans and drawings to a different scale.

q: 52. In chain surveying, perpendiculars to the chain line, are set out by
explain: An optical square, using the principle of double reflection, is the standard field instrument used to set out perpendicular offsets from a chain line.

q: 53. Profile leveling is usually done for determining
explain: Profile leveling (longitudinal sectioning) determines the elevation of points at fixed intervals along a straight line, typically for road or pipeline alignment design.

q: 54. The 'point of curve' of a simple circular curve is
explain: The point of curve (PC) is where the circular curve begins, i.e., the point of commencement of the curve from the back tangent.

q: 55. Ramsden eye-piece consists of
options: two convex lenses short distance apart
two concave lenses short distance apart
one convex lens and one concave lens short distance apart
two plano-convex lenses short distance apart, with the convex surfaces facing each other
explain: A Ramsden eyepiece consists of two plano-convex lenses of equal focal length placed a short distance apart with their convex surfaces facing each other, reducing spherical and chromatic aberration.

q: 56. Designation of a curve is made by
options: angle subtended by a chord of any length
angle subtended by an arc of specified length
explain: In practice (as per the book's answer key), a curve is designated by its radius, though in many other references degree of curve (angle subtended by a standard chord) is also used.

q: 57. For the locating a distant object visible from two transit stations, the method usually preferred to, is
options: angles and distance from transit stations
angle from one transit station and distance from the other
explain: For a distant, inaccessible object visible from two transit stations, the method of intersection (angles observed from both known stations) is generally preferred since distances to the object are unknown/inaccessible.

q: 58. The most reliable method of plotting a theodolite traverse is
options: by consecutive co-ordinates of each station
by independent co-ordinate of each station
by plotting included angles and scaling off each traverse
by the tangent method of plotting
explain: Plotting by independent (total) co-ordinates of each station, computed from a common origin, is the most reliable method since errors do not accumulate progressively as they would with consecutive co-ordinates.

q: 59. The orthographical projection of a traverse leg upon the reference meridian is known as
explain: The projection of a traverse leg onto the north-south reference meridian (parallel to the meridian) is called its latitude.

q: 60. The co-ordinate of a point measured perpendicular to the parallel is called
explain: The perpendicular distance of a point from a reference meridian, measured parallel to the parallel (east-west), is called the meridian distance (or total departure) of that point.

q: 61. Total latitude of a point is positive if it lies
explain: By convention, latitude is taken as positive (northing) when the point lies north of the reference parallel, and negative (southing) when south.

q: 62. The altitude of a traverse leg is obtained by multiplying its length by
explain: Latitude of a traverse leg = length x cosine of its reduced bearing, since latitude is the projection along the north-south meridian direction.

q: 63. In a closed traverse, sum of south latitudes exceeds the sum of north latitudes and the sum of east departures exceeds the sum of west departures then, the closing line will lie in
explain: If the net latitude is southward and the net departure is eastward, the closing error vector points south-east, so the closing line to balance it lies in the opposite (north-west) quadrant.

q: 64. The operation of making the algebraic sum of latitudes and departures of a closed traverse, each equal to zero, is known
explain: Adjusting all latitudes and departures so their algebraic sums each equal zero (removing closing error) is collectively known as 'balancing the traverse'.

q: 65. If the angular measurements of a traverse are more precise than its linear measurements, balancing of the traverse, is done by
explain: The transit rule is used when angular measurements are more precise than linear measurements, distributing closing error in proportion to the latitude/departure of each leg rather than its length.

q: 66. The branch of surveying in which both horizontal and vertical positions of a point, are determined by making instrumental observations, is known
explain: As per the book's answer key, this branch is designated 'tachemetry' (an alternate spelling of tacheometry), the surveying method that determines both horizontal and vertical positions instrumentally without chaining.

q: 67. The method generally preferred to for contouring an undulating area, is
explain: For undulating terrain, tacheometric surveying is preferred for contouring because it allows both horizontal distance and elevation to be obtained quickly and accurately from a single instrument station.

q: 68. A line joining some fixed points on the main survey lines, is called a
explain: A tie line joins two fixed points on main survey (chain) lines and is used to take offsets for detail near those points and provide an additional check.

q: 69. A base line in a chain survey
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the survey or locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixes up the directions of all other lines
explain: The base line is the principal, most accurately measured line of the chain survey framework - it fixes the directions of other lines, enables location of details, and checks the overall accuracy, so all listed functions apply.

q: 70. A plumb bob is required
options: when measuring distances along slopes in a hilly country
for accurate centering of a theodolite over a station mark
for testing the verticality of ranging poles
explain: A plumb bob is a versatile tool used for centering instruments, checking verticality of poles, and transferring points down slopes - so all the listed uses are valid.

q: 71. Chain surveying is most suitable when
options: area to be surveyed is small
ground is fairly level and open with simple details
plans are required on a large scale
explain: Chain surveying works best under a combination of favourable conditions - small area, level open ground with simple details, and large-scale plan requirements - so all of these apply together.

q: 72. The degree of the curve is the angle subtended by a chord of ... length
explain: In the metric system commonly used in this text, the degree of curve is defined as the angle subtended at the centre by a chord of 25 m (some systems use 30 m for peg intervals; the book's answer key specifies 25 m for degree of curve).

q: 73. If L is the specified length of a tape, L1 its actual length and S the measured distance, then true distance is given by the formula
explain: As per the book's answer key, the true distance correction formula given is ((L-L1)/L) x S, representing the proportional correction applied for the discrepancy between nominal and actual tape length.

q: 74. Metric chains are generally available in
explain: Standard metric chains used in India/Nepal and similar countries are commonly manufactured in 20 m and 30 m lengths.

q: 75. The method of finding out the difference in elevation between two points for eliminating the effect of curvature and refraction is
explain: Reciprocal leveling, by taking observations from both ends of a line and averaging, eliminates the combined effects of earth curvature and atmospheric refraction.

q: 76. While measuring with a metallic tape of 30 m length pull should be applied
explain: For a standard 30 m metallic tape, a pull of about 3 kg (the same as the standardizing pull) is typically applied during measurement to maintain accuracy.

q: 77. The ratio of the distances at which a stated length can be distinguished by the telescope and the human eye, respectively, is called
explain: Resolving power of a telescope refers to its ability to distinguish fine detail, defined by the ratio of distances at which a stated length can be resolved through the telescope compared to the naked eye.

q: 78. The first reading from a level station is
explain: The very first reading taken after setting up a level at any new position is always a back sight, used to determine the height of the instrument.

q: 79. Bergchund is a topographical feature in
explain: Bergchund/bergschrund-type terrain features are associated with hilly/mountainous topography, as per the book's classification.

q: 80. A check line in a chain surveying
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the surveyor to locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixed up the directions of all other lines
explain: A check line, by connecting two known points on the main framework and being independently measured, checks accuracy, helps in locating interior details, and helps verify directions - so all of the above apply.

q: 81. A tie line in a chain surveying
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the surveyor to locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixed up the directions of all other lines
explain: A tie line serves multiple purposes in chain surveying - checking accuracy, locating interior details, and helping fix directions - hence all of the above apply, similarly to a check line.

q: 82. Then the position of a point is to be located accurately by a perpendicular offset, the direction of perpendicular is set out by means of
explain: To accurately set out a perpendicular offset direction from a chain line, an optical square (based on double reflection) is the standard instrument used.
